title: Assert on the returned htmx fragment, not just the status

facts.note: Test files are identifiable by path/file kind.
Bun test files are TS/JS; language alone does NOT establish the stack (see next fact).

Activation prerequisite: the repository/test belongs to the Bun/htmx stack (e.g. test runner is bun:test and the app serves htmx fragments). Needs a stack observer; the rule is Bun/htmx-specific and has no counterpart in other stacks.

Per-test-case AST analysis: the case performs a real HTTP request (e.g. fetch against the served app). A direct unit call of a handler function that returns a Response without performing an HTTP request does NOT satisfy this fact.
Detector finding (htmx_tester_detector): case asserts on status or ok and never reaches .text()/.json()/toContain/toMatch/markup assertion.

fires: In a Bun/htmx stack test file, a test case fetches an htmx endpoint over HTTP, asserts expect(res.status).toBe(200) and ends without reading the body.
In a Bun/htmx stack test file, a test case performs an HTTP request and asserts only on res.ok, with no .text(), .json(), toContain or toMatch on the response.
doesNotFire: A test case that performs no HTTP request, including a direct unit call of a handler that returns a Response and asserts its status.
A test case that performs an HTTP request but never asserts on status or ok.
A test case that asserts on status/ok and also reaches the body via .text(), .json(), or a markup matcher.
Test suites outside the Bun/htmx stack (the rule has no counterpart in other stacks' tester extensions).

given: In a Bun/htmx stack test, a test case performs an actual HTTP request (not a direct handler call) and asserts on the response status or ok
when: the tester writes or changes that test case
then: The test case MUST also assert on the response BODY; reaching the body in any form (.text(), .json(), a markup matcher) satisfies the rule.
prefer: For htmx fragments, make the body assertion check the fragment contract (hx-attributes, ids later oob swaps target, structure), as in the example above.
avoid: Status-only tests: asserting expect(res.status).toBe(200) or res.ok and stopping — proves the route exists and nothing about what the user will see.
unless: The case does not perform an HTTP request (out of scope).
The case never asserts on status (out of scope). Note: asserting on res.ok counts as a status assertion, so an ok-only case is in scope.
why: In a JSON API the contract is the payload and status plus a parsed field is a complete test; in htmx the contract is the markup (hx-attributes, ids later oob swaps target, structure) swapped into the live DOM. A status-only test misses a refactor dropping an id a sibling's hx-swap-oob needs, which fails silently at runtime (see coder.htmx.swap-oob-carries-id).
evidence: Every Bun/htmx test case that performs an HTTP request and asserts on status/ok also reaches the body via .text(), .json(), or a markup matcher (toContain/toMatch/markup assertion).
htmx_tester_detector reports zero findings for the changed test files.
verifier_detail: Flag a test case that fetches, asserts on `status`/`ok`, and never reaches `.text()` / `.json()` / a `toContain` / `toMatch` / markup assertion.
Reaching the body in any form — `.text()`, `.json()`, a markup matcher — satisfies the rule.
Skip cases that perform no HTTP request (including direct handler unit calls returning a Response); skip cases that never assert on status (status or ok).
Term status_only_test: a case asserting on status or ok and never reaching the body; it proves the route exists and nothing about what the user will see.
Term fragment_contract: the returned markup itself — hx-attributes, the element ids later out-of-band swaps target, and the structure. In htmx this IS the interface, where a JSON API has a payload.
Scope: Bun/htmx stack test files only.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

Bun/htmx-specific obligation with no counterpart in any other stack's tester extension; it exists because the stack moved the contract from the payload into the markup — the clearest case in this extension of an obligation that could not have been inherited from another stack.
Statement says realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector`; implementation block says validator ref `htmx_tester_detector` (naming discrepancy retained for auditors).
Original name: 'htmx endpoint tests assert on the returned fragment'.
Severity 3; disposition strict (atdd-bun fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline).
